A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are sufficiently readable to compare, including matching retained proofs across renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 report original Gaussian simulations and Waterbirds experiments. Appendix S.3 provides additional background-specific experimental results.

after.justification: Sections 6–7 and Figures 1–4 report original simulation and Waterbirds results, including comparisons with the added label-shift baseline and ViT-16 features.

M1.justification: The proposed KL distribution-matching estimator, target predictive probabilities, and weighted empirical risk minimization remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 removes the step estimating the background-specific benchmark ξ1; this concerns the comparator rather than the proposed adaptation procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four-dimensional Gaussian mixture and Waterbirds classification problem with the same missing source subgroup. CelebA remains an illustration rather than an evaluated dataset. Added encoders and allocation rates change experimental settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Naive2, the label-shift correction γ(x) that ignores background A, alongside the retained source-only benchmark, now called Naive1. This expands the central comparisons in both synthetic and Waterbirds experiments. The separate ξ1 and ξ0 subgroup comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: Section 6 changes the stated synthetic protocol from known generating probabilities and known subgroup proportions to quantities estimated through Algorithm 1. Waterbirds adds a ViT-16 feature configuration and allocation rate a=0.3, retaining ResNet-18 and a=0.5/0.7. The synthetic results therefore should not be interpreted as same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: v3 removes the A=1-specific simulation and Waterbirds evaluations and the A=0-specific Waterbirds analyses in v2 Appendix S.3. It adds an encoder comparison and extends allocation sensitivity to a=0.3, documenting conditions where the proposed estimator underperforms the naive benchmarks.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 simulations per synthetic configuration and 50 repetitions per Waterbirds configuration, using boxplots to display variability. There is no change in seed disclosure, confidence-interval reporting, or significance-testing practice.

E6.justification: The empirical result displays are substantially replaced: v3 reports new γ(x), ViT-16, and a=0.3 results while removing background-specific entries. Section 7 changes the reported finding from consistent superiority to superiority in most scenarios, with losses at extreme allocations visible in Figure 4. Synthetic distributions also change under the revised stated protocol.

T1.justification: v3 Section 4.1 adds the mathematical definition of γ(x) under the background-agnostic label-shift assumption. The proposed method's identifiability results, consistency and generalization bounds, moment-matching alternative, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged. The downstream-risk equations are relocated into Section 5.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: recovering target predictions despite a missing source subgroup, estimating proportions through distribution matching, theoretical guarantees, and empirical benefits. The emphasis on recovering performance for the unobserved subgroup remains in the contribution list and conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 explains why greater representation of the observed A=1 subgroup helps, and why near-absence of additional subgroups can cause failure. Section 8 adds a substantive applicability boundary: new target background categories create an OOD identification problem beyond the paper's scope. These qualifications were absent from v2.

D1.justification: v3 documents the added ViT-16 configuration as using frozen ImageNet-pretrained features, alongside the retained ResNet-18 and L2-regularized logistic regression details. It removes v2's explicit 0.5 classification-threshold disclosure; this omission does not establish that the threshold changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through new discussions distinguishing the problem from imbalanced and few/zero-shot learning, and arguing that adversarial alignment can collapse missing subgroups onto observed ones. New references also cover label-shift inference and causal invariance. The existing OSLS/PU relationship remains; DANN and ADDA are discussed rather than experimentally evaluated.

P1.justification: The eight-section narrative remains recognizable. Changes include systematic replacement of 'prediction models' with 'predictive probabilities,' localized benchmark and experiment rewrites, moving former Section 4.5 into Section 5, and adding impact and acknowledgment text. Author information and appendix naming are also updated.

P2.justification: The empirical figures are extensively reconstructed: synthetic comparisons are consolidated into one figure, and Waterbirds panels are reorganized by encoder and allocation rate with three-method legends. Background-specific appendix plots disappear. The TMLR format also changes typography, front matter, captions, and page layout throughout; the three tables are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added label-shift comparator, encoder comparison, and explicit failure conditions make v3's empirical assessment more informative and its applicability easier to judge. The gain is limited: removing background-specific results weakens support for the retained claim about the unobserved subgroup, and implementation disclosure remains sparse. The central method and theoretical guarantees are essentially unchanged.
